newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran urges closer ties with Saudis against U.S..
newsitem.headline: Iran urges closer ties with Saudis against U.S..

text.p: Iranian state radio called on Tuesday for closer ties between Iran and Saudi Arabia to foil what it called "plots" by the United States to undermine their relations.
"Developing economic and political cooperation (with Saudi Arabia) is necessary now, more than ever, to foil plots by the regional countries' common enemy (U.S.)," Tehran radio said.
It was commenting on the current visit to Saudi Arabia by Iran's commerce minister.

Iran has rejected media reports that it was linked to the bombing of a U.S. military complex in Saudi Arabia in June that killed 19 American airmen. Some Tehran officials have said the reports indicated that Washington was preparing to attack Iran.
The radio said Iran could provide Saudi Arabia with know-how and goods cheaper than Western equivalents.
Expanded economic ties would help foil "plots by foreigners to disrupt the two countries' relations," it said.

Iran's ambassador to Saudi Arabia, in remarks published by Tehran newspapers on Tuesday, said Saudi authorities had agreed to admit 5,000 Iranian pilgrims a week, up from 3,000, for the umra -- the "minor pilgrimage" to Mecca performed round the year separately from haj, the major annual Moslem pilgrimage.
He said this showed that ties between the two countries had entered a "new phase".

Saudi Arabia and its Gulf Arab allies often have tense relations with their non-Arab neighbour Iran. They have accused Tehran of interfering in their internal affairs and voiced concern over its arms buildup.
Tehran has denied the charges, saying Washington is creating a fear of Iran in the region to sell more arms to its rich Gulf Arab allies.
